scope: Exact deterministic closure algebra and solver checks. Not a statistical power study, FDR/SupFDR simulation, Rust test, or proof of the underlying compound-process assumptions.
algorithm: Sort compound scores once; prefix sums; binary search threshold count q_r for each r; scan for the largest certified r. O(n log n).

all_subset_closure_equivalence.result: Direct enumeration of every nonempty intersection matched the exact positive-part deficit condition in every case.

exhaustive_solver_vs_bruteforce.result: The O(n log n) solver matched brute-force maximum cardinality, retained the baseline e-BH set, and satisfied closure.

randomized_solver_vs_bruteforce.result: All selected cardinalities and closure conditions matched exhaustive search.

neutral_zero_padding.result: Appending one zero-score candidate did not change the selected prefix of any pre-existing candidate.

future_high_score_extension_witness.interpretation: An appended high-scoring candidate can change an old candidate's decision. The local certificate and global weights are horizon-independent, but arbitrary high-score extension of the rejection set is not.

execution_note: These checks were run in a local Python exact-rational reimplementation of the committed functions. The committed unittest suite is authored for independent reproduction but was not run by GitHub Actions. No Rust build or test was performed.
claim_boundary: The exact closure identity and finite solver are deterministic results. The SupFDR guarantee remains conditional on globally valid time-monotone base e-processes, common filtration, fixed global weights, source-only reserve caps, and forward-only transfers. No statistical superiority or SOTA claim.
